On November 17, 2026, all authors participated in the ninth hackathon for the Research Support Handbook. For this hackathon, we mostly worked on **Tools documentation**, but completed a few other updates as well.

## Overview of results

With respect to tools, we did the following:

- We updated the OSF information to align it with current developments at OSF, namely the termination of OSF Projects
- We added termination information for a number of tools (SciStor and SciCloud), more will follow
- The Qualtrics documentation has been restructured so that it better aligns with documentation about the other tools
- We updated the list of ADA maintainers
- We updated some SciSure information
- We removed information about winscp from the Yoda documentation
- We're working on a compute guide, this will be published soon

We [checked external links](https://github.com/ubvu/open-handbook/pull/976) and found a number of broken links, which have all been repaired now.

Some other stuff we worked on:

- The Data Horror Stories, which used to be on the VU website, have been transferred to the {{< var title >}}. You can now find them in the footer of the website. If you need an example to showcase the importance of good data management practices, you can use those.
- We used to have a reference to the GHOST Collective (the group of people working on serious games for Open Science) in the footer, but this information is now included in the [trainings overview](https://rdm.vu.nl/trainings.html#ghost-collective)
- We updated the policies page with the new VU Strategy (2026-2030) and the VU Research Strategy (2023-2033)
